details: RADRUE (Realistic Analytical Dose Reconstruction Utilizing Estimates): Monte Carlo dose reconstruction model developed by Cardis et al. (NCI/IARC) for the UkrAm/BelAm thyroid cancer study; reconstructs individual doses for 110,645 Ukrainian and 69,595 Belarusian liquidators; uses: (1) individual interview data on location and tasks; (2) job-exposure matrices (JEM) by work type × time period × location; (3) published and measured dose rates by location × time; (4) Monte Carlo uncertainty propagation; output: individual mean dose (Sv) + geometric SD; 95% of doses in range 0-400 mSv; mean ~117 mSv Ukrainian liquidators
chernobyl_application: RADRUE was the methodological backbone for: Tronko 2006 BMJ (thyroid cancer); Zablotska 2013 Environ Health Perspect (leukemia); Hatch 2005 NCI cohort description; Thyroid cancer ERR/Gy = 1.91 derived directly from RADRUE dose assignments; leukemia ERR = 1.52 from same cohort; dose reconstruction took 2003-2007 for primary analysis; RADRUE represents most rigorous retrospective dose reconstruction in radiation epidemiology history
source: Cardis 2005 J Radiol Prot doi:10.1088/0952-4746/25/3/R01; Likhtarev 1994 Health Phys; Drozdovitch 2007 Health Phys; unscear_liquidator_doses_REAL.csv; nci_ukraine_thyroid_cohort_REAL.csv

details: RADRUE four input streams: (1) Individual interview questionnaires: location by month; work tasks (driving; bulldozing; roof decontamination; construction; dosimetry monitoring); protective equipment used; (2) Job-Exposure Matrix (JEM): dose rate by task × location × period; derived from >5000 measured dose rates in CEZ 1986-1990; (3) Ambient dose rate data: Soviet monitoring records; retrospective dosimetry (EPR tooth enamel; FISH chromosomal aberrations for subset); TLD/film badge records (known to be unreliable for high doses); (4) Official badge data: used with quality adjustment factor because of documented underreporting (badge cap 35 rem for most of 1986)
chernobyl_application: JEM construction: > 60 job categories defined; dose rates assigned per: proximity to Unit 4; date of work (radioactive decay reduces rates over time); type of location (roof of Unit 3 = highest; distant village decontamination = lowest); key challenge: roof workers (biorobots) had short duty cycles (40-90 seconds per person) at extreme dose rates (0.1-5 Gy/minute measured); their total dose estimated from: number of trips × duration × measured rate; badge records for roof workers found to be most severely underestimated (badges confiscated post-work at some sites); individual thyroid measurement (400,000 performed 1986) = most accurate biomarker available for internal dose component

details: RADRUE dose uncertainty: geometric standard deviation (GSD) = 2.0-3.5 per individual; meaning: 95% confidence interval spans ÷2.0 to ×2.0 for best cases (GSD=2.0); or ÷3.5 to ×3.5 for worst cases; sources of uncertainty in order of magnitude: (1) recall bias in interview data: work location recall after 15-20yr = GSD 1.5-2.0 component; (2) spatial heterogeneity of dose field: factor 5-10 variation within single work zone = GSD 2.0-3.0; (3) temporal variation: dose rates changed rapidly April-August 1986 = GSD 1.5; (4) JEM applicability to individual: GSD 1.3-1.5; combined GSD: 2.5-3.5 for most individuals
chernobyl_application: Human factors remain largest uncertainty source (factor of 3) in all Chernobyl dose reconstruction: even with best available models, individual dose uncertainty spans order-of-magnitude range for high-exposure workers; this uncertainty is SYSTEMATIC in the dose-response direction (underestimation likely → true ERR/Gy may be LOWER than estimated if doses are underestimated); RADRUE specifically modeled uncertainty probability distribution as log-normal → Monte Carlo propagation of lognormal uncertainties → confidence intervals on ERR/Gy reported as likelihood profiles; see Cardis 2005 for full uncertainty methodology
source: Cardis 2005 J Radiol Prot; Simon 2006 Radiat Prot Dosimetry; retrospective_dosimetry_methods_REAL.csv

details: Electron Paramagnetic Resonance (EPR) tooth enamel dosimetry: radiation-induced radical (RO•) in hydroxyapatite crystal; signal permanent → archival dose record; detection limit: ~34 mGy for 1g enamel sample; precision: ±15-20 mGy (1σ) for absorbed tooth enamel dose; conversion to whole-body effective dose requires: geometry factor (external vs internal); tooth shielding correction; dental X-ray correction (XR adds to signal); dose rate at tooth position vs gonadal/bone marrow; Ukrainian cohort: EPR dental dosimetry performed on 2,800 liquidators and 300 evacuees (Sholom 2000; Skvortsov 2000 studies)
chernobyl_application: EPR validation: compared to TLD records → EPR higher in 60-70% of liquidators with available badge records → confirms systematic underestimation by official dosimetry; EPR for evacuees: dose reconstruction corroborated external dose estimates from contamination maps; EPR cannot distinguish fractionated vs acute dose (signal is cumulative); cannot measure internal doses; cannot distinguish neutron from gamma (though neutron contribution to most liquidator doses negligible); EPR became gold standard for evacuee retrospective dosimetry > 0.1 Gy; below ~100 mGy: uncertainty exceeds signal (GSD > 2); see retrospective_dosimetry_methods_REAL.csv
source: Sholom 2000 Radiat Meas; Jacob 1999 J Environ Radioact; retrospective_dosimetry_methods_REAL.csv

details: FISH chromosome aberration dosimetry: Fluorescence In Situ Hybridization (FISH) paints chromosome arms; detects stable translocations (persist for life = cumulative dose record) vs conventional Giemsa (detects unstable dicentrics = recent dose only); calibration curve: dicentrics per cell = 0.024 × D (Gy) + 0.078 × D² (for acute exposure); for chronic exposure: linear term dominates; FISH translocation frequency: f = (1 - e^(-D×0.04)) for linearized chromosome painting; can detect: cumulative exposures down to ~0.1 Gy; high-dose exposures up to ~3-4 Gy (saturation above); performed on 500-2000 cells per individual (scoring intensive)
chernobyl_application: FISH dosimetry in Chernobyl liquidators: Sevan'kaev 2005 (n=>1000 liquidators); translocation frequencies: 0.5-2× natural background in most liquidators; small subset 2-5× natural background = consistent with >500 mGy; compared to RADRUE estimates: good agreement for group means; poor agreement for individuals (expected given biological variation); FISH provides GROUP MEAN dose validation rather than individual dose precision; important cross-check for RADRUE model calibration; FISH results consistently higher than official Soviet badge records → confirms underestimation
source: Sevan'kaev 2005 Radiat Environ Biophys; Hande 2003 Am J Hum Genet; Lucas 2000 Cytogenet Cell Genet; retrospective_dosimetry_methods_REAL.csv

details: Soviet dosimetry falsification/limitation: documented cap at 35 rem (350 mSv) for most of 1986 liquidators; reasons: (1) official Soviet limit was 35 rem total; workers reaching 35 rem would be pulled from work; (2) supervisors falsified records to keep workers productive; (3) pocket ionization chambers (KID-2) often lost or confiscated; (4) dose rates in some areas exceeded DP-5 maximum range (200 R/hr) → meter read as zero; (5) film badges: processing and calibration variable; cumulative underestimation factor: EPR studies show TLD/badge records underestimate by factor 1.5-3 on average (range 1.1-10); for roof workers: underestimation may be 5-15×
chernobyl_application: Practical consequence for dose-response studies: Cardis 2005 RADRUE specifically corrected for badge underreporting using: (a) EPR subsample as calibration; (b) documentary evidence of 35 rem cap; (c) JEM dose rate data independently; RADRUE doses are systematically higher than official records → ERR/Gy estimates may be LOWER than simple badge-based analyses would suggest (doses higher → same cancer excess → lower ERR/Gy); this is conservative direction for radiation risk assessment (ERR/Gy potentially lower = less risk per unit dose); see also: Guskova Hospital No. 6 records = most reliable because clinical dosimetry (lymphocyte nadir)
source: Ivanov 2001 Am J Ind Med; Bebeshko 2008; retrospective_dosimetry_methods_REAL.csv; chernobyl_first_responders_medical_REAL.csv

details: Liquidator dose distribution (RADRUE-based): Ukrainian cohort (n=110,645): mean = 117 mSv; median = 87 mSv; geometric mean = 86 mSv; GSD = 2.3; distribution: lognormal; 95th percentile ~450 mSv; 99th percentile ~900 mSv; estimated <1% received >1 Sv; ~50 individuals received >5 Sv (acute high-dose workers); Belarusian cohort (n=69,595): mean ~80 mSv; Russian cohort (n=~200,000 RNMDR): mean ~105 mSv (RNMDR data); ~600,000 total liquidators: collective dose ~60,000-80,000 person-Sv; timeline: 1986 (year 1) = highest dose rate period (~50% of collective dose delivered)
chernobyl_application: 1986 liquidators received ~3-4× higher individual doses than 1987-1990: (1) higher residual contamination; (2) less protective equipment initially; (3) most dangerous tasks first (roof clearing; sarcophagus construction foundations); 1987 onwards: better dosimetry; less hazardous tasks; lower contamination; collective dose 60,000-80,000 person-Sv × cancer risk 5%/Sv = projected 3,000-4,000 excess cancer deaths in liquidator population lifetime (though many already diagnosed)
source: Cardis 2005; Ivanov 2004 PMID:15141805; UNSCEAR 2008; unscear_liquidator_doses_REAL.csv; liquidator_health_outcomes_REAL.csv

details: Soviet thyroid dose measurements 1986: Soviet authorities performed ~400,000-500,000 thyroid measurements using external gamma detectors on evacuated populations; measured I-131 activity in thyroid (Bq); used to reconstruct internal thyroid dose; problems: (1) many measurements performed May-June 1986 when I-131 substantially decayed (t½=8.02d; ~3-5 half-lives by May-June) → already 8-32× lower than peak; (2) measurement equipment calibration variable; (3) geographic coverage uneven; (4) records largely lost/destroyed or never transferred from Soviet to Ukrainian/Belarusian archives; only ~15,000 measurements with adequate documentation for use in dose reconstruction studies
chernobyl_application: RADRUE thyroid dose component: uses available 1986 measurements + milk contamination data + stable iodine status correction + ICRP dosimetry model; estimated thyroid doses: median 0.1-0.3 Gy for evacuated children; range 0.01-30+ Gy; doses to Belarusian pre-schoolers: 26% received >5 Gy thyroid dose (Likhtarev data); compare: external dose to same population ~10-50 mSv; thyroid dose was 2-3 orders of magnitude higher than external for most young children → explains why thyroid cancer = only confirmed large-scale radiogenic solid cancer; see unscear_evacuee_thyroid_doses_REAL.csv
source: Likhtarev 1995 Radiat Environ Biophys; Gavrilin 1999; unscear_evacuee_thyroid_doses_REAL.csv; iodine_atmospheric_chemistry_REAL.csv

details: RADRUE validation against biological dosimetry: EPR comparison: RADRUE group mean doses within 10-25% of EPR group means → validates JEM approach at group level; individual Pearson correlation r=0.35-0.55 → moderate individual agreement (expected given uncertainties); FISH comparison: group mean translocation frequencies consistent with RADRUE doses; individual correlation r=0.4-0.6; JEM self-consistency check: dose rates by task category consistent with published Soviet monitoring data where available; retrospective ecological comparison: cancer risk in subgroups correlated with RADRUE dose groups → dose-response confirmation
chernobyl_application: RADRUE is the gold standard specifically because it: (1) does not rely exclusively on falsified Soviet badge records; (2) incorporates multiple independent data streams; (3) propagates uncertainty explicitly; (4) has been validated against biological dosimetry; alternative dose assessment (Kesminiene 2008 Estonian study using official records): ERR/Gy lower → confirms RADRUE's correction for badge underestimation improves accuracy; RADRUE approach subsequently used for Fukushima worker dose reconstruction (modified for different exposure conditions)
source: Cardis 2005; Zvonova 2002; Kesminiene 2008 Radiat Res; fukushima_chernobyl_comparison_REAL.csv
